# v0.1.3

The bus check now runs where the adapter actually is.

It lived in `scripts/`, so it only existed on a checkout of this repository —
while the USB RS-485 adapter is plugged into the machine Home Assistant runs
on. Running it meant copying the repository onto the server and installing
pymodbus there.

It now ships with the integration. After installing, it is at
`/config/custom_components/mennekes_amtron/smoke_modbus.py`, and it imports
nothing from the integration, so it runs as a plain script with Home
Assistant's own Python — which already has pymodbus, because the integration
requires it.

```bash
# Home Assistant OS, Supervised or Container
docker exec -it homeassistant \
  python /config/custom_components/mennekes_amtron/smoke_modbus.py \
  /dev/serial/by-id/<your-adapter>

# Home Assistant Core in a virtual environment
/srv/homeassistant/bin/python \
  /config/custom_components/mennekes_amtron/smoke_modbus.py \
  /dev/serial/by-id/<your-adapter>
```

On Home Assistant OS, open a shell with the *Advanced SSH & Web Terminal*
add-on and turn its protection mode off, otherwise the add-on cannot reach
`docker`.

## Searching for the wallbox

If the device address or the baud rate was changed with the MENNEKES
configuration tool, let the check find them:

```bash
... smoke_modbus.py /dev/serial/by-id/<your-adapter> --scan --scan-baudrate
```

`--scan` tries every documented address from 10 to 50, `--scan-baudrate` every
documented baud rate as well, and it prints how long that will take before it
starts.

## Also

The check reports the EVSE state in words and tells you which values to enter
in the config flow. The quickstart now gives the exact command per
installation type, for finding the adapter and for running the check.

It is still strictly read-only: it sends no heartbeat and writes nothing, so
it cannot put the wallbox into the energy-manager error state.
